page.title: How to Choose a Hybrid Event Production Company
page.description: Learn what hybrid production covers, how to vet vendors, what to ask before signing, and what timelines and budgets look like for room-and-stream events.
page.h1: How to choose a hybrid event production company
page.definition: A hybrid event production company is a crew that runs the physical room and the live stream as one show, handling cameras, encoding, run of show, speaker rehearsal and backup stream so both audiences get the same experience.
page.quick_answer: Ask for a run of show from a past hybrid event, confirm they bring their own encoder and backup stream, and lock venue AV and platform six to eight weeks out.

sections.h2: What does a hybrid event production company actually do?

blocks.p: A hybrid production company owns the run of show for both the room and the stream, supplying cameras, switcher, encoder, graphics, speaker rehearsal, live producer, moderation and a backup stream.

ul: Run of show with cues for in-room and remote audiences
Speaker brief and rehearsal on the real platform
Branded slide template and lower thirds
Live producer calling cues and managing Q&A
Hardware encoder and redundant backup stream
Edited recording and highlight clips delivered within twenty-four to forty-eight hours

sections.h2: How do you tell if a vendor can run the room and the stream together?

blocks.p: Look for a single crew that rehearses speakers on the real platform, brings a hardware encoder, and shows a run of show with cues for both in-room and remote audiences.

head: Capability
Virtual vendor
Hybrid operator
rows: Owns run of show for both audiences

sections.h2: What should you ask before signing a contract?

blocks.p: Ask for a recent hybrid run of show, who operates the platform on show day, how they handle a stream failure, and whether they quote per production or per day.

ol: Share a run of show from a comparable hybrid event
Name the platform operator and show caller for show day
Explain the backup stream failover process
Confirm deliverables: recording, clips, transcript, analytics
Clarify pricing model: per production or day rate plus expenses
Define who owns registration, follow-up and CRM handoff

sections.h2: How much does hybrid production cost?

blocks.p: Moderated webinars typically run two thousand five hundred to seven thousand five hundred per production, while executive summits and hybrid conferences start at ten thousand and go to fifty thousand or more depending on crew size and days.

Platform and production are two purchases: the platform is software; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream. West Peek Productions produces events on the platform you choose and can help you choose it; it does not sell event software.

sections.h2: What timeline do you need to plan a hybrid conference?

blocks.p: Plan six to eight weeks out, lock venue AV and platform before the agenda is final, run one full rehearsal two to five days before, and do a technical check sixty minutes before going live.

ul: Week one to two: intake, brief, platform and venue AV locked
Week three to four: speaker briefs, slide template, run of show draft
Week five: full rehearsal on real platform with all speakers
Show day: technical check sixty minutes before, live producer on site
Post-show: replay and clips within twenty-four to forty-eight hours

faq.q: Can we use our existing webinar platform?
faq.a: Yes. Production crews work on Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24, StreamYard or the platform you already licence. They bring the encoder, cameras and run of show; you keep the platform contract.
The production company focuses on show day. Registration lives in Eventbrite or Cvent, follow-up in HubSpot or Salesforce. Confirm who owns each handoff before the event.

faq.q: Do we need a separate AV vendor for the room?
faq.a: A hybrid crew brings cameras, switcher and encoder for the stream. The venue often supplies in-room sound, screens and lighting. Clarify the split in the contract so nothing falls through.

faq.q: How fast can we get a replay?
faq.a: Send the edited recording and clips within twenty-four to forty-eight hours while attendees still remember the event. Ask for this deliverable in the scope.
